exposure: Late pregnancy haemoglobin A(1C) (HbA(1C)) at 29-30 weeks of gestation
finding: Elevated late pregnancy HbA(1C) levels at 29-30 gestational weeks were associated with an increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm delivery, Caesarean section, LGA, neonatal respiratory distress, neonatal hypoglycaemia, and composite adverse neonatal outcome.
